headline: Diesel Falls Below $6, but the Global Fuel Crisis Is Far From Over
facebook_description: American diesel prices fell below $6 per gallon for the first time in two months, reaching $5.998 nationally according to GasBuddy data reported by Reuters. But depleted inventories and disrupted global refining capacity continue to pressure fuel supplies. Lower crude prices do not necessarily translate into cheaper diesel when refineries cannot meet demand. Trucking, agriculture and construction businesses remain exposed to elevated fuel costs, which can affect consumers through freight and product prices.
